newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on liquidity concern.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on liquidity concern.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed moderately lower on Tuesday over concerns that high money rates due to tight liquidity in the banking system would prevent additional funds from entering the stock market, brokers said.
The weighted index finished 21.25 points or 0.27 percent lower at 7,887.36.
Turnover was a frantic T$149.49 billion.
Before Tuesday the index had risen more than 1,000 points in 1997, attracting a huge amount of funds from the banking system and causing recent sharp growth in money rates.
The overnight interbank rate had hovered above a relatively high eight percent in recent days and was still at 7.836 percent at mid-session on Tuesday, despite the central bank's fund injections.
"The tight liquidity level prompted some investors to sell their shares in the stock market," said Allen Huang, fund manager for National Securities.
"The stocks' recent sharp gains made the market an easy target for profit-taking," Huang added.
The recently hot electronics sector fell by 0.56 percent.
Chipmaker Mosel Vitelic lost T$1 to T$42.70 and Primax Electronics dropped T$1.50 to close at T$73.
Buying focused on cheaper shares in construction and paper sectors. The paper index rose 2.38 percent while construction scrips gained 0.98 percent.
Brokers said the market largely ignored the January industrial output and export order figures announced by the government on Tuesday morning.
The industrial output rose 6.01 percent in January compared to a year ago. Export orders rose 2.03 percent year-on-year.
Brokers expected the market to consolidate at the current level on Wednesday.
